title: Left completeness and a uniform upper bound on lower truncations
statement: Let C and D be abelian categories with unbounded derived categories, K-injective resolutions, and exact countable products [def-sp-abelian, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-category-product]. Every K in D(C) is the homotopy limit, with the specified canonical projections, of its standard truncation tower tau_{>=-n}K [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category, def-weil-derived-limit]. Consequently, if G:D(C)→D(D) is triangulated and preserves countable products, and G(tau_{>=-n}K) lies in D^{<=b} for every natural n, then G(K) lies in D^{<=b+1}. No bound on K itself or heart objects is assumed.

source.place: Statement and proof; existing Lean realization lean/WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/LeftComplete.lean: isHomotopyLimit_truncGECone and isLE_obj_of_forall_isLE_obj_truncGE

proof.text: Form the tower of standard lower truncations tau_{>=-n}K and its canonical cone. Exact countable products give products in D(C) and let homology commute with them. Form the distinguished fibre triangle of 1 minus the transition shift on the product of this tower.

source.place: Proof of left completeness: the truncation tower and its Milnor triangle

proof.text: In degree i the tower is zero before max(0,-i) and its cone maps are isomorphisms thereafter. A cone on such a tower is limiting: lift at the first stable index and use its inverse. The endomorphism 1 minus shift is split epic: its section has nth component minus the sum of the input components from the first stable index to n-1, transported through the stable cone maps. The kernel is therefore H^i(K). The long exact sequence of the fibre triangle and this kernel calculation make K to the fibre an isomorphism on every homology object, hence an isomorphism. Thus K with its specified truncation projections is a homotopy limit.

source.place: Proof of left completeness: the eventually constant homology tower

proof.text: A triangulated functor preserving countable products sends that triangle to the Milnor triangle of its images. If all these images lie in D^{<=b}, their product does too, since target homology commutes with products. Rotating the triangle once expresses G(K) between a product shifted by -1, in D^{<=b+1}, and the unshifted product, in D^{<=b}. Extension closure gives G(K) in D^{<=b+1}.

source.place: Left completeness and products: the uniform truncation-bound consequence
